gap: No result ChatGPT got shows how to string the 8 × 450 W panels in a complete 48 V kit: 8 in series gives 8 × 35.03 V = 280.2 V Voc, which is under the inverter's 500 V series limit, while two strings of 4 give only 4 × 30.08 V = 120.3 V Vmp at STC. Which layout works depends on the inverter's MPPT window and per-input current limit, so the shopper has to settle that before wiring.
standout_why: ChatGPT's searches returned no results, so there was no rival page to compare against. ChatGPT's own two answers give rough sizing only: a 75% efficiency factor, 80% usable battery and peak-sun-hour arithmetic. Neither answer does any panel-to-inverter string arithmetic: no Voc against the 500 V series limit, no Vmp against the MPPT window, and no Isc against the per-input current limit. Neither names a kit or checks that the kit's own '14.4 kWh/day' claim is gross output with no losses. I scored this 2, not 3, because I couldn't open a page with the inverter's MPPT voltage range or per-MPPT current limit. Without those I can't show that 4-in-series falls below the MPPT minimum, which is what would make the wiring finding decide the set.
kit_items: Complete kit (inverter + battery + panels in one cart): Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E. It is one SKU on one approved store (awin:sungoldpower) and Dealectric already lists it. It pairs an 8,000 W 48 V 120/240 V inverter with built-in dual MPPT (no separate charge controller), 2 × 51.2 V 100 Ah SG48100P LiFePO4 (10.24 kWh) and 8 × 450 W N-type panels (3,600 W).

Panel strings: wire all 8 panels in one series string. Using SunGold's SGN-450-BDG5 figures, that is Voc 280.2 V at STC, under the manual's 500 V series limit and leaving about 220 V for cold-weather Voc rise. Don't assume two strings of 4: Vmp is only 120.3 V, and current doubles to 32.1 A Isc if both go on one input.

Battery: the included 10.24 kWh (2 × 51.2 V × 100 Ah) covers about 0.8 day at ChatGPT's 10 kWh/day example. Each extra SG48100P adds 5.12 kWh. The listing says the batteries support up to 63 in parallel.
Not in the kit and not sourced here: PV disconnect/combiner, DC breakers between battery and inverter, MC4 extension cable, and racking.

findings.label: Maker's daily-energy claim, checked
findings.value: 14.4 kWh/day gross; about 10.8 kWh/day at a 75% system factor
findings.note: Listing: 'approximately 14.4kWh of solar energy per day under 4 hours of full sunlight'. 8 × 450 W = 3,600 W; 3,600 W × 4 h = 14.4 kWh, so the claim includes no losses. Applying ChatGPT's own 75% factor: 14.4 × 0.75 = 10.8 kWh/day.

findings.label: Battery energy and autonomy
findings.value: 10.24 kWh nominal; about 8.2 kWh usable; about 0.82 day at 10 kWh/day
findings.note: Listing: 'two SUNGOLDPOWER 51.2V 100Ah SG48100P server rack LiFePO4 batteries', '7,000+ deep cycles', 'UL1973 and UL9540A'. 2 × 51.2 V × 100 Ah = 10.24 kWh. The 80% usable figure is ChatGPT's assumption, not the maker's: 10.24 × 0.8 = 8.19 kWh, and 8.19 / 10 kWh/day = 0.82 day. ChatGPT's 2-day example would need about 25 kWh, roughly 3 more SG48100P.

findings.label: Inverter PV and charge headroom
findings.value: Up to 11,000 W PV input on dual MPPT; up to 180 A combined solar + AC charging
findings.note: 3,600 W of kit panels / 11,000 W = 33% of rated PV input, so about 7,400 W of panels could be added before the inverter limit (subject to the per-MPPT limits in unsourced). Full-array charge current is about 3,600 W / 51.2 V = 70 A, well under 180 A.

findings.label: PV series-string voltage limit
findings.value: Open-circuit voltage of PV panels in series must be below 500 V
findings.source_title: Sun Gold Power SPH8K48SP User Manual (All-in-one solar charge inverter V3.0)
findings.note: Manual quote: 'The open circuit voltage of PV panel in series connection must below 500V'; rated output 8,000 W, 120/240 Vac. String arithmetic with SGN-450-BDG5: 8 × 35.03 V = 280.2 V Voc (OK, 220 V margin for cold rise). Maximum at STC is 500 / 35.03 = 14.3, so 14 panels; cold correction lowers that, but I didn't source the temperature coefficient. 4 in series: Vmp 4 × 30.08 = 120.3 V. Two 4-panel strings on one input: Isc 2 × 16.05 = 32.1 A. A search tool said the kit's inverter is the SPH8048P rather than SPH8K48SP; I couldn't confirm that from the kit page (HTTP 429).

unsourced: Inverter MPPT operating voltage range (125–425 V according to search summaries) and max PV input current per MPPT (22 A according to search summaries).
